system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: we largely follow the CLAUDE.md rules file published there with similar agent workflow for a single agent, but we modify it for the agentic and bounty setting. The summary of these modified rules (234 lines)
system_prompt_style.note: A fixed rules file (CLAUDE.md) given to each agent; per-agent identity/bounty parameters suggest templating.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agents interact directly with the interactive proof system: they can invoke tactics, inspect proof states and goals, analyze tactic successes and failures, and iteratively refine their proof scripts.

observation_format.evidence_quote: we modified the error messaging so that the agents are more clearly informed about their mistakes

tool_call_format.note: Underlying agents are Claude Code and Codex; harness-level tool call format not described.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: they can invoke tactics, inspect proof states and goals, analyze tactic successes and failures, and iteratively refine their proof scripts
loop_primitives.note: Proof-checker feedback drives repair; checking by Megalodon is the verifier.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Agents can lock a theorem by paying 10% of its bounty (max 10 locks, 24h each), reserving the right to collect the full bounty if completed.
planning_granularity.note: The shared file of bounties/locks acts as a persistent structured task list.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Four agents compete for the theorem bounties (45k “simulated USD” tokens total) but are incentivized to collaborate to finish early and earn bonuses.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Agents can issue sub-bounties, solve others’ bounties, and strategically choose between cooperation and competition to maximize total and personal earnings.
delegation_mechanism.note: Coordination via the shared git repository/bounty file and TODO comments, not a spawn mechanism.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: are also ready to step in as admins if we see a major problem later
human_in_loop.note: Human admins intervene ad hoc (e.g. resetting Charlie's balance); no formal gating point.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: enforces immutability of definition and theorem statements (while allowing proof modifications), precisely tracksQed vs. Admitted, validates lock persistence and expiry more robustly, checks balance transitions
short_term_state.note: Balances, locks and bounties form a typed shared state beyond messages.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: the agents would leave comments for themselves, such as TODO Bob show <some property>
long_term_memory.note: Persistent repository file with TODO notes and the CLAUDE.md rules file.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: regular backups, and careful progress tracking
state_persistence.note: Git commits/backups serve as checkpoints; explicit resume path not described.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Megalodon is an interactive theorem prover/proof checker based on higher-order Tarski-Grothendieck set theory.
self_verification.note: The Megalodon proof checker checks .mg files automatically on each commit or push through a GitHub action. The line number is not available in the excerpts. The paper also mentions local guard scripts that agents must run before committing; those are closer to action policies. The value was flagged not_in_enum by the first reading; formal is the closest fit.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: This prompt is repeatedly given to the agent until it converges in about 8 hours (producing 32 backups)

rollback.evidence_quote: Frequent pull–commit–push cycles are mandatory, locks must be pushed immediately, and guard tools must confirm no rule violations before committing.
rollback.note: Git is the shared store; agents are told to avoid reverting or losing work.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: announcing (after several debugging and double-checking runs) that it is not aware of any possible issues
termination_condition.note: Overall experiment ended when LLM subscription usage was depleted.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Four agents compete for the theorem bounties (45k “simulated USD” tokens total)
cost_controls.note: Simulated token budget is an incentive mechanism, not a real spend cap; real limits came from subscription quotas.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Agents can lock a theorem by paying 10% of its bounty (max 10 locks, 24h each)
timeouts.note: 24h lock expiry is the only time limit described; no tool-level timeout reported.

execution_isolation.note: Agents run the Megalodon checker locally; no container/VM isolation described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: never edit outside the AlgTop section
filesystem_access.note: Scoping enforced by rules and guard scripts rather than the filesystem.

permission_model.evidence_quote: we use local guard scripts that agents must run before committing
permission_model.note: Guard scripts check invariants (balances, locks, statement immutability) before commits; not a per-action allowlist.

tracing.evidence_quote: We tracked the bounty lifecycles over the course of the experiment by detecting when a theorem first entered a Bounty state and when it later transitioned to a Collected state.
tracing.note: Git commit history serves as the structured record analysed in Figs. 1-2.

replayability.evidence_quote: Fig. 1 shows the formalization size over the run of the experiment.
replayability.note: No replay facility described; only commit history is preserved.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: All accepted proofs are ultimately checked and verified by the underlying proof assistant.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation is via the external Megalodon checker plus manual line counting; no benchmark runner in the repo evidence.

guardrails.evidence_quote: enforces immutability of definition and theorem statements (while allowing proof modifications)
guardrails.note: Guard scripts block rule-violating commits; the Qed command is also blocked for partially proved dependencies.

target_domain.evidence_quote: We describe an experiment in large-scale autoformalization of algebraic topology in an Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP) environment, where the workload is distributed among multiple LLM-based coding agents.

open_source.evidence_quote: The evolving public repository is athttps://github.com/mgwiki/alg_top.
open_source.note: Public repository; licence not stated in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: using two ChatGPT Pro Codex 5.3 models and two Claude Code (Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6) models

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: The evolving public repository is athttps://github.com/mgwiki/alg_top.
primary_artifact.note: Repo is the formalization output, not harness code; coded from the paper.

first_release_date.note: Basis: paper v1 date (no tagged release available).

stars.note: Star count is for mgw_test, the repo supplied in the evidence; alg_top count not given.
